answer: A wharf only lets a ship dock after it posts a bond that is forfeited if it breaks the rules. An agent economy can do the same: each identity must lock a stake before it can earn, and the stake is slashed when the same operator is caught running duplicates, proven by overlapping work trails, like two statues carved from one block of marble or layers of shale from a single quarry. One identity costs little; a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, so Sybil farming stops paying.
